title: José Aldo Returns to Combat Sports in a Grappling Fight
seoTitle: José Aldo Returns to Combat Sports in Grappling Fight
subtitle: The UFC Hall of Famer will make his first combat‑sports appearance since retirement.
excerpt: UFC legend José Aldo announced his comeback in a grappling match on October 4, marking his first combat‑sports appearance since retiring.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
José Aldo, legendary UFC fighter and Hall of Famer, will make his return to competition on October 4. The announcement, made by Aldo himself on Thursday, marks his first appearance in combat sports since his UFC retirement.

The Return to Combat Sports

The former UFC featherweight champion is slated to face Marlon Vera, a former UFC bantamweight title challenger, in a submission grappling bout. The fight will headline a Hype FC card in Quito, Ecuador.

Aldo ended his UFC career after a loss to Aiemann Zahabi at UFC 315. His UFC run was highlighted by a dominant reign in the featherweight division for years, before his defeat to Conor McGregor in 2019, which ended his reign. Since then he has stayed involved with the sport, following recent developments such as Max Holloway’s victory over McGregor at UFC 329.

The Opponent: Marlon Vera

Marlon Vera, known as “Chito,” comes into the grappling showdown on a four‑fight losing streak. His most recent loss was a unanimous decision to David Martinez in February. Prior to that, Vera also fell to Sean O’Malley at UFC 299.

Despite the grappling bout, Vera has a UFC Octagon return scheduled for next month. He will face Charles Jourdain at UFC 331, an event that will feature Joshua Van vs. Alexandre Pantoja 2 as the main event. Vera previously competed in a Hype FC grappling match that ended in a draw against UFC featherweight Jean Silva.

José Aldo’s Legacy in the UFC

José Aldo is widely regarded as one of the greatest fighters in UFC history and, for many, the promotion’s best featherweight ever. He holds the UFC record for most consecutive featherweight title defenses, with seven. Notable victories include wins over Chad Mendes, Frankie Edgar and Urijah Faber.

Although he has suffered defeats to Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway in his career, his status as a sport legend is undeniable. Fighter Jorge Masvidal, for example, still considers Aldo the number‑one featherweight of all time, highlighting his skill in every fighting position, his jiu‑jitsu and his impressive wrestling offense and defense.

A Possible Permanent Return?

Aldo’s appearance in submission grappling raises questions about the future of his combat‑sports career. Sources indicate it is still unclear whether this will be a broader comeback or a one‑off event. Nonetheless, the announcement has already generated huge interest, placing José Aldo’s name among the most talked‑about topics.

With information from boxingnews.com, BJPenn.com, MMA Junkie.
